key_insight: Agents-K1 shifts scientific knowledge handling from simple paper retrieval to agent-native knowledge orchestration. Instead of only using abstracts and citation links, it structures papers into entities, claims, evidence, mechanisms, and method lineages for deeper reasoning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap in current LLM-based research agents that can orchestrate tasks but still fail to organize scientific knowledge in a way that supports real research reasoning. Existing systems often flatten papers into abstracts and cite graphs, losing the structure needed to understand how ideas, evidence, and methods connect.
method: Builds an end-to-end pipeline that converts raw documents into structured scientific knowledge.
Extracts and organizes key components such as entities, claims, evidence, mechanisms, and method lineage.
Creates knowledge representations designed specifically for agent use, enabling more reasoning-aware retrieval and orchestration.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means research agents can become more useful for literature review, hypothesis generation, and method comparison because they work with richer scientific structure. It can improve reliability and depth in agent-driven research workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing raw papers transformed into structured knowledge
Knowledge graph with nodes for claims, evidence, entities, and methods
Before-vs-after comparison: flat abstracts/citations vs agent-native orchestration
Icon set for paper, magnifying glass, graph nodes, and reasoning chain
paper_authors: Zongsheng Cao, Bihao Zhan, Jinxin Shi, Jiong Wang, Fangchen Yu
